name: PayPal Design System
summary: Recreate PayPal's dual-blue institutional wallet UI — balance card, activity feed, and soft-pill CTAs — as a paste-ready SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures PayPal's dual-blue brand system, PayPal Sans type ladder, soft-pill button geometry and rich-icon activity feed so an agent can generate on-brand wallet screens.

whatYouGet: A complete PayPal-accurate color, type and component reference an agent can build from without guessing hex codes or spacing
House rules that keep the dual-blue wordmark, soft-pill buttons and tabular activity feed consistent across every screen it generates
A structured brief template so you can point the same prompt at any wallet/payments screen and get a matching result
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in recreating the visual language of major fintech apps with pixel-level fidelity. You have shipped production wallet and payments UI and you obsess over consistent token usage, tabular numerals, and soft-elevation card systems.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light mode):
- PayPal Blue #003087 — primary CTA fill, active tab, wordmark ink
- PayPal Sky #0070BA — secondary accent, link color, icon tint
- PayPal Cobalt #001C64 — deepest blue, reserved for splash/illustration backgrounds only
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Gray #F5F7FA (section fills), Surface Gray 2 #EEF1F4 (input fill), Divider #E5E8ED
- Text Primary #001435 (near-black with a blue cast, never pure black), Text Secondary #2C2E2F, Text Muted #687173, Text Tertiary #9DA3A6
- Semantic: Success Green #1C8B43 / bg #E4F5EA, Error Red #D20021 / bg #FCE5E8, Warning Amber #FFB81C
- Activity icon colors: Sent = #003087, Received = #1C8B43, Card = #0070BA, Reward = #FFB81C
- Dark mode: canvas #0A0E1A (blue-tinted, not pure black), surface #141A2A / #1F2740, PayPal Blue shifts to #3B82F6 for contrast

Typography: PayPal Sans Big (display/headings/buttons/amounts) + PayPal Sans Small (body/metadata); Inter is the closest free substitute with tabular-nums enabled everywhere a $ amount appears.
- Balance hero: Big 36pt/700, tracking -0.5pt, tabular
- Send-amount hero: Big 56pt/700, tracking -1pt, tabular
- Screen title: Big 24pt/700; Section header: Big 18pt/700
- Activity title 15pt/500 (Small), activity subtitle 13pt/400 (Small), activity amount 16pt/500 (Big), tabular
- Button label: Big 17pt/700

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48; standard horizontal margin 16pt; card padding 20pt. Radius scale: 4pt (pills/badges), 8pt (text fields, modal container), 12pt (wallet item cards), 16pt (balance card, filter chips, sheet top corners), 24pt (primary CTA — a soft pill, radius = half of its 48pt height), full pill (search bar). Shadows: card 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); floating 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.10); sheet 0 -8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.20).

Named distinctive patterns:
1. The dual-blue "P-P" wordmark — two overlapping italic P's, Sky behind, Blue in front, NEVER rendered as one flat color
2. Balance card anchor — white card, 16pt radius, label → 36pt tabular balance → Add Money / Transfer pill row
3. Activity row with colored circular transaction-type icon (68pt min height) and tinted status pills (Completed/Pending/Failed/Refunded)
4. Send Money fullscreen amount entry with a live-updating "Send $X.XX" CTA and a restrained checkmark success screen (no confetti)
5. Activity filter chip row (All/Sent/Received/Pending/Card/Refunds), 32pt height, 16pt radius
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never render the P-P wordmark in a single color — the Sky-behind/Blue-front overlap is non-negotiable brand identity.
2. Text Primary is always #001435, never pure #000000 — the slight blue warmth is deliberate.
3. Every $-amount, percentage, or share-style figure must use tabular numerals so vertical columns of prices align exactly.
4. Primary CTAs are soft pills where radius equals half the button height (48pt tall → 24pt radius) — never sharp corners on a primary action.
5. Reserve green and amber exclusively for semantic status (success/pending) — never use them as decorative or primary brand accents.
6. Activity-row icons are colored by transaction type (Sent=Blue, Received=Green, Card=Sky, Reward=Amber) and must never be flattened to monochrome gray.
7. Keep shadows gentle (0.06–0.10 opacity) — PayPal reads as a lifted card wallet, not a flat tech product and not a heavy skeuomorphic bank app.
8. Activity rows must never drop below 64–68pt tall — the rich icon plus two lines of text needs the room.
9. Reserve PayPal Cobalt (#001C64) strictly for splash screens and illustration backgrounds, never for interactive UI.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Ledger — a peer-to-peer bill-splitting app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Home wallet tab + activity feed + send-money flow"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "balance, 3 sample transactions with names/amounts/dates"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Send, Request, Add Money, filter activity by status"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [both / light only]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the dual-blue system but swap in our own product name/wordmark shape"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above (light + dark), named clearly and grouped by role.
2. A `Font` extension mapping the two-tier PayPal Sans system onto Inter/SF Pro fallbacks, matching every size/weight/tracking row in the hierarchy table.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the balance card, an activity row (with the colored icon + status pill), and the primary/secondary pill buttons.
4. The Send Money fullscreen amount-entry screen with the live-updating CTA text and the restrained success screen.
5. The bottom tab bar and activity filter-chip row, wired to the active/inactive color rules.
6. A short checklist mapping each of the house rules to where it was applied in the generated code, so I can verify nothing drifted from spec.
</what_to_give_me>

Run it in Claude or your AI assistant of choice
Paste the generated SwiftUI tokens/components into your project and adjust to your actual brand constraints

name: Revolut Design System

description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures Revolut's dark-canvas gradient system, Aeonik type ladder, metal-card motion and spend-analytics donut so an agent can generate on-brand banking screens.

whatYouGet: A complete Revolut-accurate dark-mode color, type and elevation reference so generated screens never drift into a generic dark theme
House rules that protect the gradient-as-sole-accent rule and the signature card-flip/spend-donut interactions
A structured brief template so you can retarget the same prompt at any account/cards/analytics screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in premium dark-mode fintech interfaces. You have shipped production banking apps with gradient brand systems and understand how to keep a single accent gradient disciplined across an entire dark UI without it becoming noisy.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark-native — canonical):
- Canvas #0A0A0F (cool near-black, never pure black or warm)
- Surface 1 #16161F (cards, tiles), Surface 2 #1E1E2A (sheets, active rows), Surface 3 #28283A (pressed/track)
- Divider #2A2A38, Border Subtle #33334A
- Brand Gradient #5B6BFF → #9C6BFF (~115°) — the entire brand color story; solid fallback #6B5BFF for thin strokes/small icons/focus rings only; pressed #5648D6
- Text Primary #FFFFFF, Text Secondary #9A9AAA, Text Tertiary #6A6A7E
- Semantic: Income Green #1FD17B, Spend Red #FF5A6A, Warning Amber #FFB23F, Crypto Gold #F7C948, Info Blue #3F9BFF
- Light mode exists but is secondary: canvas #FFFFFF, surface #F4F4F8, text #0A0A0F, brand solid #5648D6 (no gradient ghosting)

Typography: Aeonik (proprietary geometric grotesque); Inter is the closest free substitute. Tabular figures mandatory on every balance/amount/currency-tile figure.
- Balance hero: 40pt/700, tracking -0.6pt
- Screen title: 28pt/700; Section header: 22pt/700; Tile balance: 22pt/700
- Amount (row) and merchant name: 16pt/600
- Body: 15pt/400; Button: 16pt/600; Tab label: 10pt/600 fixed
- Negative tracking scales from -0.6pt at hero size down to 0pt at body — never apply the gradient to text glyphs, it is a fill/stroke device only

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit, scale up to 64pt; 16pt screen margin; 20pt card padding; transaction rows separated by hairlines with 0pt gap. Radius scale: 8pt (chips/tags), 12pt (inputs/small tiles), 16pt (buttons/cards/metal-card hero), 20pt (analytics cards), 24pt (sheet top corners). Elevation is deep on a dark ground: card shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 8px 24px; a signature gradient glow rgba(108,91,255,0.30) 0 8px 28px sits under the primary CTA and active states.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Metal-card hero carousel — ISO-ratio card, 16pt radius, brushed-metal gradient with a diagonal sheen that sweeps on appear; tap triggers a Y-axis 3D flip (~450ms) revealing CVV/expiry, with a confirming haptic
2. Spend-analytics donut — single ring, gradient-filled spent arc over a #28283A track, center total + "this month" label, category legend below
3. Multi-currency balance stack — flag-chip tiles with tabular right-aligned figures, decimal-aligned across a horizontal or vertical carousel
4. Live FX ticker strip — mid-market rate with a 60s refresh and a small green/red delta arrow
5. Gradient CTA glow — the primary button casts a soft violet ambient halo, described as the brand "lit from within"
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The violet-to-purple gradient is the entire brand accent — never introduce a second brand hue, and never apply it to text glyphs (fill/stroke only).
2. Canvas must stay a cool near-black (#0A0A0F) — never pure #000000, never warm-toned.
3. Balances and amounts are always tabular and decimal-aligned; incoming transaction amounts are #1FD17B, outgoing are #FFFFFF, never swapped.
4. The balance is the single largest element on any screen it appears on — 34-40pt weight 700.
5. Give the metal-card hero its full signature treatment (sheen sweep + 3D flip + haptic) whenever a card object is requested — don't flatten it to a static image.
6. Float every surface off the canvas using elevation (deep shadow) and radius, not heavy borders.
7. Keep the donut and sheen animations smooth and singular (700ms / 1.2s) — never aggressive or looping distractingly.
8. Aeonik/Inter never drops below weight 400 — no light or thin weights anywhere in the system.
9. Show live FX rate transparency wherever a currency conversion happens — never hide the delta.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Nomad — a multi-currency travel card app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Home with metal card hero + spend donut + currency stack"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "3 currencies, sample spend categories, one card design"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Exchange, freeze card, view statement"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [dark-first / both]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the gradient system but shift hue to our brand's teal-to-blue"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above (dark-native + light variant), grouped by role.
2. A `Font` extension mapping the Aeonik/Inter hierarchy with correct tracking values at each size.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the metal-card hero (with sheen + 3D flip modifier) and the spend-analytics donut card.
4. The multi-currency balance tile/carousel and a transaction row component with correct income/spend coloring.
5. The gradient primary CTA with its ambient glow shadow, plus pressed/disabled states.
6. A short checklist mapping each house rule to where it was applied, so I can verify the gradient discipline held throughout.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Robinhood Design System
summary: Recreate Robinhood's flat white brokerage UI — giant portfolio chart, scrubber, and green/orange directional color — as a paste-ready SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures Robinhood's radically simple chart-first layout, Capsule Sans type ladder and green/orange direction system so an agent can generate on-brand investing screens.

whatYouGet: A complete Robinhood-accurate color, type and elevation reference that keeps the app's signature flatness rather than defaulting to generic card shadows
House rules that lock in the green=up/orange=down direction binding and the black (not green) Trade button convention
A structured brief template so you can retarget the same prompt at any portfolio/position/order screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in brokerage and trading apps. You have shipped production stock-charting UI and understand how a radically flat, chart-first layout communicates trust through simplicity rather than institutional heaviness.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, canonical):
- Canvas #FFFFFF, Surface Gray #F7F7F7, Surface Gray 2 #EFEFEF, Divider #E6E6E6
- Robinhood Green #00C805 (up movement, buy CTA within trade flow, profitable positions) — pressed #00A904, background tint #E6F9E0
- Robinhood Red #FF5000 — this is actually a saturated ORANGE, not red, used for down movement and sell CTA; background tint #FFEDE5
- True Error Red #E62232 reserved only for hard errors (order failed), kept visually distinct from the orange loss color
- Warning Yellow #FFB800, Info Blue #1D6FF2 (sparingly, educational links)
- Crypto accents: Bitcoin Orange #F7931A, Ethereum Purple #627EEA
- Text Primary #000000 (true black — deliberate, not softened), Text Secondary #5C6166, Text Tertiary #9B9EA3
- Dark mode: canvas #000000 (true black), surface #181B1F/#23272D, green stays #00C805 (reads electric on black)

Typography: Capsule Sans Text (body/UI) + Capsule Sans Display (hero portfolio values 40pt+); Inter with tabular-nums is the closest free substitute.
- Portfolio hero: Display 40pt/700, tracking -0.5pt, tabular
- Day-change line: Text 16pt/500, colored green or orange, no background chrome
- Screen title: 22pt/700; Position title (company name): 16pt/600
- Ticker symbol: 13pt/500, tracked +0.3pt (treated as a branded micro-monogram)
- Position value/change: 17pt/500 and 13pt/500, both tabular
- Button: 16pt/600; Tab label: 10pt/600 fixed

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit, scale to 64pt; 16pt horizontal margin; 32pt gap between major sections, 16pt between rows. Radius scale: 4pt (badges), 8pt (primary buttons, modal containers, news cards), 12pt (search bar), 16pt (sheet top corners), 24pt (full modal top corners). Shadows are almost absent: subtle card lift is only rgba(0,0,0,0.04) 0 2px 6px; sheets use rgba(0,0,0,0.12) 0 -6px 24px — the chart line is the only real visual lift in the whole app.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Full-bleed portfolio chart with a real-time drag scrubber — dragging updates the hero portfolio value live and shows a solid black value bubble at the touch point, no smoothing, 60fps
2. Chart-range chip row (1D/1W/1M/3M/YTD/1Y/5Y/ALL) — text-only, active chip flips to the chart's direction color with a 2pt underline
3. Day-change pill that is NOT a pill at all — just colored inline text with no background chrome
4. The universal Trade button is BLACK with white text, never green — green/orange are reserved exclusively for Buy/Sell inside the trade modal
5. Order-placed success screen — green confetti burst + Capsule Sans Display "Order Placed" text
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Color is always bound to direction: green (#00C805) never appears on a down number and orange (#FF5000) never appears on an up number.
2. Use the true error red (#E62232) only for hard system/order failures — keep it visually distinct from the orange loss color at all times.
3. Every price, percentage and share count must render in tabular numerals so vertical columns align as the user scans a list.
4. The universal Trade button stays black with white text — green and orange belong only to Buy/Sell inside the trade modal, never to the general CTA.
5. Keep shadows at or below 0.04-0.12 opacity everywhere — Robinhood is essentially flat, and the chart line is the app's only real visual lift.
6. Track ticker symbols (AAPL, GOOGL) at +0.3pt letter spacing — treat them as branded micro-monograms, not plain text.
7. Use pure #000000 for primary text, not a softened gray — this is a deliberate clean tech-product choice.
8. Never crowd position rows below 56pt tall — data density is already at its practical limit.
9. The day-change line is inline colored text only — never give it a pill background or border.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Ledger Trade — a fractional-shares investing app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Home portfolio chart + position list + buy/sell modal"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "portfolio value, 5 sample positions with tickers/shares/day-change"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Buy, sell, set alert, view chart ranges"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [both / light only]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the flat chart-first layout but swap the green/orange pair for our own direction colors"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above (light + dark), including the true-red-vs-loss-orange distinction clearly commented.
2. A `Font` extension mapping the Capsule Sans Text/Display hierarchy onto Inter with tabular-nums enabled.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the portfolio hero block plus a working chart-scrubber gesture (drag updates hero value live).
4. A position row component and the chart-range chip row with the direction-colored active state.
5. The Trade button (black) plus the Buy/Sell modal buttons (green/orange), and the order-placed success screen.
6. A short checklist mapping each house rule to where it was applied, so I can verify no color/direction rule was inverted.
</what_to_give_me>

name: SoFi Design System
summary: Recreate SoFi's dark-navy, pill-shaped member dashboard — gradient net-worth hero, product tile grid, cross-sell cards — as a SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures SoFi's navy-canonical brand system, Manrope type ladder, fully-pill button geometry and consolidated tile-grid dashboard so an agent can generate on-brand member screens.

whatYouGet: A complete SoFi-accurate navy/gradient color, type and elevation reference so generated screens read as a wealth dashboard, not a generic dark theme
House rules that lock in the pill-everything geometry and the colored performance/sub-stat conventions across tiles
A structured brief template so you can retarget the same prompt at any member-home/banking/invest screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in multi-product wealth-membership apps. You have shipped production banking-plus-investing dashboards and understand how to make a consolidated net-worth view feel organized rather than overwhelming.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (navy-native — canonical in both themes):
- Navy Canvas #0A0E27, Surface 1 #121736 (tiles/cards), Surface 2 #1B2147 (elevated/pressed), Divider #252C55
- Light mode: canvas #F4F7FB, surface #FFFFFF/#EEF2F8, divider #E2E7F0 — brand identity still stays navy + blue
- SoFi Blue #00A0DF (brand base, gradient start), Blue Bright #29C2FF (accents/links/active tabs — brightened so it pops on navy), Blue Pressed #0086BC
- Member-hero gradient: #00A0DF → #1B53C4 → #0A0E27 (~165°), blending into the navy canvas
- Text Primary #E8EBF7 (navy) / #0C1330 (light), Text Secondary #9BA3C7 / #5A6286, On-Blue Ink #042235 (near-black blue text on solid blue buttons)
- Performance: Positive/Gain #2FD08A, Negative/Loss #FF6B6B (coral, never a harsh red), Rewards Gold #F2C14E — performance IS color-coded here, unlike a pure spending app

Typography: Manrope as the faithful free stand-in for SoFi's brand-tuned geometric sans. Numbers are always weight 700-800 and tabular.
- Net worth hero: 40pt/800, tracking -1.2pt, tabular
- Screen title: 32pt/800; Section header: 22pt/700
- Tile value: 18-19pt/700, tracking -0.4pt, tabular
- Card title: 16pt/700; Body: 16pt/400
- Row title: 15pt/700; Amount: 15pt/800 tabular
- Caption/sub-stat: 12pt/600; Tab label: 10pt/600 fixed

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit up to 64pt; 16pt inset for tiles, 20pt for headers/gradient content; 2-column tile grid with 12pt gap. Radius scale: 11-12pt (icon chips/small fills), 16pt (cross-sell cards/sheets), 18pt (account/product tiles — the signature tile radius), 24pt (large promo/sheet tops), 500pt (full pill — EVERY button and chip). Elevation: tiles lift with a 1pt #252C55 border + rgba(0,0,0,0.25) 0 2px 12px shadow; the gradient hero itself IS the strongest elevation cue (color reads as depth).

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Member hero gradient panel — full-bleed #00A0DF→#1B53C4→#0A0E27 diagonal wash carrying the net-worth figure in white plus a green month-change pill ("+$1,840.22 this month")
2. 2-column account/product tile grid — Banking, Invest, Loans, Card — each an icon chip + value + a colored sub-stat (green gain, coral due-date, gold rewards)
3. Cross-sell product cards in a horizontal carousel — "one member, many products" is the business model made visible
4. Fully pill-shaped buttons (500pt radius) everywhere — primary, secondary, and soft variants alike
5. Net-worth count-up animation and a gradient-parallax scroll (~0.7x) on the hero
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Treat navy (#0A0E27) as the canonical brand canvas in BOTH light and dark mode — it is not merely a dark-mode fallback.
2. Every button and chip is a full pill (500pt radius) — never render a boxy or sharp-cornered control anywhere in this system.
3. Performance is deliberately color-coded (gains green, losses coral, rewards gold) — never neutralize it, since showing performance is the point of a wealth app.
4. Brighten blue to #29C2FF for any accent, link, or active-tab use so it reads clearly against navy — the base #00A0DF alone can look dull on dark.
5. Net worth is always the loudest element on the member home — 40pt weight 800 white on the gradient, never buried below tiles.
6. Surface cross-sell product cards prominently wherever relevant — hiding them contradicts SoFi's core multi-product business model.
7. All net-worth, balance and percentage figures are heavy (700-800 weight) and tabular so the wealth picture stays instantly scannable.
8. Lift tiles off navy with a 1pt #252C55 border plus a soft dark shadow — never rely on shadow alone on a dark ground.
9. Never drop the rewards-gold accent from the rewards/points loop — it is a stated brand pillar, not decoration.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Meridian — an all-in-one banking, investing and lending membership app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Member home with net-worth hero, tile grid, cross-sell carousel"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "net worth, 4 product tiles (banking/invest/loan/card), 2 cross-sell cards"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Transfer, invest now, view loan payment schedule"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [both, navy-canonical]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the pill-everything geometry but recolor the gradient to our own brand hue"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above (navy-native + light), grouped by role.
2. A `Font` extension mapping the Manrope hierarchy with correct tracking at hero/title/tile sizes.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the member hero gradient panel (with net-worth count-up + change pill) and the 2-column product tile grid.
4. A cross-sell product card component in a horizontal snap carousel.
5. The fully-pill primary/secondary/soft button variants and the bottom tab bar.
6. A short checklist mapping each house rule to where it was applied, so I can verify the navy-canonical + pill-everything rules held.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Venmo Design System
summary: Recreate Venmo's social payments feed — emoji memos, mixed-weight feed lines, and the Pay/Request split pill — as a SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures Venmo's feed-first social layout, Venmo Sans type ladder and signature Pay/Request pill so an agent can generate on-brand social-payments screens.

whatYouGet: A complete Venmo-accurate color, type and component reference that keeps the social-feed framing rather than defaulting to a plain transaction list
House rules that protect Venmo's privacy model (no public amounts) and the emoji-as-signal convention
A structured brief template so you can retarget the same prompt at any feed/pay/confirmation screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in social-consumer payments products. You have shipped production feed-based UIs and understand how to make a financial transaction read as a small social story rather than a ledger entry.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, canonical):
- Canvas #FFFFFF, Surface Muted #F7F7F7, Divider #F2F2F2, Divider Strong #E0E0E0
- Venmo Blue #008CFF — the single defining brand color (bright and friendly, explicitly NOT a banking navy), Deep Blue pressed #0078DE, Blue Tint #E6F4FF
- Blue gradient (hero-only): linear #008CFF → #0078DE, used on signup/onboarding/checkmark confirmation
- Text Primary #2F3033 (warm charcoal, not pure black), Text Secondary #6B6E76, Text Tertiary #9AA0A8
- Semantic: Received Green #4BB543, Charge Red #D32E2E (sent amounts render neutral charcoal, not red — red is reserved for errors/destructive), Pending Orange #F5A623
- Dark mode: canvas #1A1A1A, surface #242424/#2E2E2E

Typography: Venmo Sans (weights 400/600/700) for UI + Venmo Display for hero numbers (balance, confirmation amount, sign-up headline). Dollar sign is always glued to the number with no space ("$24.50" not "$ 24.50").
- Balance display (Me tab): Display 56pt/700, tracking -0.8pt
- Amount input hero (Pay screen): Display 72pt/700, tracking -1.0pt
- Payment confirm amount: Display 44pt/700
- Feed transaction line and memo: Sans 15pt/400 (names within the line render at 600 — mixed weights inline)
- Amount (activity): Sans 17pt/700, tracking -0.1pt, tabular
- Timestamp: 13pt/400; Tab label: 11pt/600 fixed

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit up to 72pt; 16pt standard margin; feed row padding 12pt vertical / 16pt horizontal. Radius scale: 4pt (tag chips), 12pt (inner cards, small buttons), 16pt (sheet/modal top corners), 20pt (balance card), 22-26pt (secondary buttons, search input), 50pt/full (Pay/Request split pill, all primary CTAs). Shadows are minimal except one branded exception: the Pay/Request pill casts rgba(0,140,255,0.25) 0 4px 12px, a deliberately visible blue glow marking it as THE important action.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Feed transaction row with NO amount shown publicly — mixed-weight inline sentence ("Alex paid Jordan · 2h"), an emoji-rich memo line, and an Instagram-style like/comment row beneath
2. Emoji memo as the primary "what was this for" signal — rendered at native system emoji, never re-skinned

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in high-volume retail and grocery apps. You have shipped production shopping UIs built for speed, outdoor readability, and dense product grids, and you understand why price hierarchy matters more than decoration in this category.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, canonical — bright-first, no dark-native mode):
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Tint #F2F8FD (cool-blue tinted card wells), Surface Gray #F5F5F5 (input fill/skeletons), Divider #E2E8F0, Border Strong #C9D2DE
- Walmart Blue #0071DC — the single action color: CTAs, links, active tab, filled checkbox; pressed #004F9A; tint #E6F1FC
- Spark Yellow #FFC220 — reserved ONLY for the Spark logo and savings chrome (Rollback tag, Save badge, deal-module CTA); pressed #E5A800
- Text Primary #2E2F32 (charcoal, not pure black), Text Secondary #74767C, Text Tertiary #9BA0A8
- Semantic: Success Green #1A7F37 (in stock), Savings Green #2A8703 ("you save $X"), Warning Amber #B25E00 (low stock), Error Red #D03A2D, Star Gold #FFB81C (ratings — deliberately warmer than Spark Yellow so it never gets confused with it)

Typography: Bogle (proprietary humanist sans); Inter is the closest free substitute. Tabular figures used in every price block and quantity stepper.
- Screen title: 28pt/700; Section header: 22pt/700
- Price (large): 22pt/700, tracking -0.2pt, tabular — the loudest element on any card
- Product title: 16pt/600, 2-line clamp (always visually lighter than the price)
- Was/struck price: 13pt/400 in Text Secondary; Meta/unit price: 13pt/400
- Tag/badge: 12pt/700 with slight uppercase tracking; Tab label: 11pt/600 fixed
- Spark Yellow is NEVER used as text color — only as a fill sitting behind dark charcoal text

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit up to 64pt; 16pt screen margin; 12pt card-grid gutter; 24pt section gap. Radius scale: 8pt (text inputs, small thumbnails, status pills), 12pt (product cards, category tiles), 16pt (sheets/modals), 22-24pt (CTAs, search bar, toggle, filter chips). Elevation is border-first: flat rows use only a 1pt #E2E8F0 border; only pressed/sticky/floating states earn a faint shadow (rgba(16,24,40,0.06) 0 1px 3px at rest, up to rgba(16,24,40,0.16) 0 -8px 32px for sheets) — never a heavy or dark drop shadow anywhere.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Rollback price tag — the signature savings callout, Spark Yellow fill with dark charcoal text, sitting flush above the price block (Clearance uses red fill/white text instead; Best Seller uses blue-on-tint)
2. Product card structure — square image → Rollback tag (if any) → price block (current price + struck "was" price + savings line) → 2-line title → rating stars → full-width Add to Cart pill
3. Pickup/Delivery toggle pill fixed at the top of Shop — a sliding-thumb segmented control, because fulfillment choice is treated as a first-class decision
4. Add-to-cart bump — a 260ms scale bump (1.0→0.96→1.04→1.0) plus a cart-badge pop and a soft haptic confirming the item "dropped in"
5. The six-ray Spark logomark, appearing top-left of the app bar with a brief staggered fan-in animation on cold launch
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Reserve Spark Yellow (#FFC220) exclusively for the Spark logo and savings chrome (Rollback/Save) — never use it as a second action color or for body text.
2. Always pair Spark Yellow fills with dark charcoal text (#2E2F32) — white text on yellow fails contrast and breaks the brand.
3. The price must always visually outweigh the product title on any card — 22pt weight 700 versus a lighter 16pt weight 600 title.
4. Every price and quantity-stepper figure uses tabular numerals so vertical columns of prices align.
5. Separate surfaces with a 1pt #E2E8F0 border before reaching for a shadow — shadow is reserved for press/sticky/float states only, and stays soft (6-16% opacity, never heavy or dark).
6. Use charcoal #2E2F32 for primary text, never pure #000000 — this keeps the bright canvas from feeling harsh.
7. Keep the Pickup/Delivery toggle and fulfillment ETA visible at the top of Shop — fulfillment is a primary decision, not a buried setting.
8. Confirm every add-to-cart action with the signature bump animation plus a cart-badge pop and soft haptic.
9. Keep the canvas bright white — never introduce a dark or moody canvas as the canonical experience.
</house_rules>

- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]

- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the blue-action/yellow-savings discipline but swap in our own two brand colors"]

</the_project>

name: Webull Design System
summary: Recreate Webull's dark trading-terminal UI — candlestick chart, order-book ladder, and Buy/Sell pair — as a paste-ready SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-research SwiftUI prompt that captures Webull's terminal-grade density, tabular price system and candlestick/ladder/options-chain components so an agent can generate on-brand trading screens.

whatYouGet: A complete Webull-accurate dark-terminal color, type and component reference for candlestick charts, order books and options chains
House rules that lock in tabular-everywhere pricing and the pervasive-not-timid green/red performance system
A structured brief template so you can retarget the same prompt at any quote/watchlist/trade screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in professional trading terminals. You have shipped production charting, order-book and options-chain UI and understand that density and decimal-perfect alignment are the entire point of this category, not something to soften.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark-native — the only canonical mode, no meaningful light theme):
- Canvas #0B0E11, Surface 1 #14181D, Surface 2 #1C2127, Divider #232931, Chart Grid Line #1A1F26 (nearly invisible on purpose)
- Brand gradient #1B9EFB → #20D5C4 (135°) — logo, primary Trade CTA, selected timeframe chips, paper-trading badge; on-brand text #04121C
- Text Primary #EAEEF2, Text Secondary #8B95A1, Text Tertiary #5A636E
- Performance (loud and pervasive, not sparing): Up/Bid/Call #00C076 (on-text #03150D), Down/Ask/Put #FA5252 (on-text #1B0606), Flat #8B95A1; depth/area fills at ~14% opacity of the same hues; dashed prev-close reference line in brand blue #1B9EFB
- Region note: some Asia markets invert up=red/down=green by user setting — the token names stay the same, only the mapping flips
- Alert Amber #F7A600 for halts/extended-hours/price-alert banners

Typography: Inter with tabular figures (`tnum`) enabled everywhere a number appears — the order ladder, option chain and price columns must align to the decimal, which is the defining typographic requirement of this category.
- Last price (quote screen): 32pt/800, tracking -0.6pt, colored by direction (never neutral)
- Screen title: 24pt/800; Section header: 20pt/700
- Watchlist row value: 15pt/700 tabular; Ladder/chain figures: 13pt/700 tabular
- Label (column heads): 11pt/600, uppercase, tracked +0.4pt
- Button: 15pt/800; Tab label: 10pt/600 fixed
- Line heights stay tight (1.1-1.3) to maximize data density without numbers colliding

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit, watchlist row 56pt tall, ladder rows ~26pt (dense), 18pt horizontal screen inset (chart itself is full-bleed). Radius scale: 2pt (depth bars/micro tags), 4pt (chips/badges), 6pt (buttons/inputs/order-type chips), 10pt (cards/panels/bottom sheets), 16pt (modal containers). Elevation is functional, not decorative: a 1pt #232931 border plus slight surface lift does almost all the work; only floating elements (crosshair tooltip, order-type popover, order-ticket sheet) get a real dark shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 8px 24px and up) — the chart itself never carries a shadow, it is the ground plane.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Full-width candlestick chart as the screen centerpiece — up/down colored candle bodies and wicks, near-invisible grid, a dashed brand-blue previous-close line, a timeframe chip strip below (1m/5m/1D/5D/1M/1Y), and a 1:1 crosshair-scrub gesture on touch
2. Order-book ladder (Level 2) — bid rows below a mid/spread divider, ask rows above, each with a right-anchored depth bar sized proportionally and tinted at ~14% opacity
3. Options chain — three-column Call/Strike/Put table, calls green, puts red, strike center in primary text, ATM row subtly highlighted
4. Docked equal-width Buy (green) / Sell (red) button pair on the quote screen, never separated into distant CTAs
5. Cyan "PAPER" badge marking practice-trading mode, and a brief color-flash (not a rolling digit) on every live price tick
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Dark is the only canonical mode — never design a primary light theme; a trading terminal lives in near-black.
2. Every numeric value — ladder, chain, prices, percentages — must be tabular so columns align to the decimal; this is non-negotiable in this category.
3. Performance color must be loud and pervasive across candles, sparklines, chips, ladder and buttons — never timid or sparing like a calm consumer app.
4. The brand blue→cyan gradient is reserved for brand/action/paper-badge use only — never apply it to gain/loss, which is exclusively green/red.
5. The big last price on the quote screen is always colored by direction, never rendered in neutral text.
6. Keep chart grid lines nearly invisible (#1A1F26) so candlestick data always dominates the visual field.
7. On a price tick, flash the color briefly (~250ms) rather than animating/rolling the digits — ticks are instantaneous events, not counted transitions.
8. Buy and Sell always appear as one docked, equal-width, color-coded pair — never as two separated or asymmetric buttons.
9. Respect the region setting that may invert up=red/down=green in some markets — never hardcode up=green as a universal assumption.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Ledger Terminal — a self-directed options and equities trading app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Quote screen with chart + order ladder + docked Buy/Sell"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "1 sample symbol with OHLC candle data, sample bid/ask ladder rows"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Buy, sell, switch timeframe, toggle indicators"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [dark-only, per category convention]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the terminal density but swap the brand gradient hue"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above, with the region-invertible up/down mapping expressed as a configurable pair rather than hardcoded literals.
2. A `Font` extension with tabular-figure modifiers applied by default to every numeric role.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the quote header (colored last price) and a candlestick chart view with a working 1:1 crosshair-scrub gesture.
4. The order-book ladder component with right-anchored depth bars and the mid/spread divider.
5. The docked Buy/Sell button pair and the options-chain three-column table.
6. A short checklist mapping each house rule to where it was applied, so I can verify tabular alignment and the region-invert hook are both correct.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in cross-border money-transfer products. You have shipped production multi-currency apps and understand how radical fee transparency becomes a visual design principle, not just a copy choice.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, canonical):
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Neutral #F7F7F7, Surface Sunken #EFEFEF, Divider #E5E5E5, Border Strong #D2D2D2
- Forest #163300 — the structural color: large titles, dark account hero, primary numbers, dark nav; hover/pressed #0E2200; hero surface #0E2200
- Bright Green #9FE870 — the ONLY action/highlight color, always paired with forest text and never white; pressed #8AD45C; tint #EAF9DC
- Text Primary #0E0F0C (near-black, faint warm cast), Text on Forest #FFFFFF, Text Secondary #6B6F66, Text Tertiary #9A9D95
- Semantic: Success Green #2F8F4E (distinct from the fluorescent brand green, used for readable status text like "money arrived"), Pending Amber #B5781E, Error Red #D4332B
- No blue, no secondary accent hue, no gradients anywhere — forest + bright green is the entire brand color story

Typography: Wise Sans (proprietary humanist sans); Inter is the closest free substitute. Weights run heavy where it matters — 400/600/800.
- Balance hero: 40pt/800, tracking -0.6pt, tabular, forest structural ink
- Screen title (large): 32pt/800; Section header: 22pt/800; Currency figure: 22pt/800
- Body/title: 16pt/600; Body: 15pt/400
- Label (uppercase): 11pt/800, tracked +0.6pt; Tab label: 11pt/600 fixed
- Bright green is never used as a type color — it is strictly a fill/highlight that sits behind forest text

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit up to 64pt; 16pt screen margin; 20-24pt card padding. Radius scale: 8pt (chips/flag containers), 12pt (inputs/small tiles), 16pt (buttons/cards/the fee card), 20pt (the forest hero, feature modules), 24pt (sheet top corners), full pill (≥20pt half-height for segmented controls/filter chips). Elevation is border-first and gentle: rest state uses a 1pt #E5E5E5 border; the forest hero is the one true elevated element at rgba(14,34,0,0.25) 0 12px 32px — its own depth is the system's strongest.

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Forest account hero — the single dark anchor in an otherwise bright layout: #0E2200 panel, "Total balance" label in bright green, the total in white 40pt/800 tabular, with a bright-green "Add money" affordance
2. Fee-transparency breakdown card — an itemized, vertically connected list (You send / Our fee / Amount we convert / Guaranteed rate / Recipient gets), with the final "Recipient gets" line emphasized in forest on a bright-green-tint highlight band — the product's signature "nothing hidden" device
3. Mid-market rate ticker — a slim row stating the live exchange rate plainly with a small pulsing live dot and a "guaranteed for 24h" reassurance
4. Send-money flow stepper — a numbered Recipient → Amount → Review → Pay progress rail, completed steps flipping to a bright-green check
5. Number roll-up — balances and totals visibly animate their digits into place (~500ms) on load and after a transfer
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Always pair Bright Green (#9FE870) fills with forest (#163300) text — never white on bright green, that contrast is the brand.
2. Keep exactly one dark anchor on any screen — the forest hero — never let a second panel go dark; everything else stays bright.
3. Never hide or summarize a fee — the itemized fee-transparency card with its highlighted "Recipient gets" line IS the product, not an optional disclosure.
4. State the mid-market rate plainly with a visible guarantee window (e.g. "guaranteed for 24h") — never omit or bury the rate ticker on a conversion screen.
5. Never introduce blue, a gradient, or any second accent hue — forest plus bright green is the complete brand color story.
6. Every balance, currency-row figure and fee-line value uses tabular numerals so decimals align down the column.
7. Use primary ink #0E0F0C for body text, never pure black — and reserve forest #163300 for structural/heading roles specifically.
8. Titles and totals run at weight 800 — never use a light or thin weight anywhere in Wise Sans/Inter.
9. Animate number roll-ups and transitions smoothly (200-500ms) — never abrupt or jarring motion.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [e.g. "Passport — a multi-currency freelancer payments app"]
- Primary screen(s) to generate: [e.g. "Home with forest hero + currency stack + send-money flow with fee card"]
- Key entities and sample data: [e.g. "total balance, 3 currency rows, one sample transfer with a fee breakdown"]
- Must-have actions: [e.g. "Send money, convert, add a recipient"]
- Platform/target: [SwiftUI iOS 17+, minimum device size]
- Light/dark mode requirement: [light-first with one forest anchor / both]
- Brand deviations allowed: [e.g. "keep the forest/bright-green discipline but shift to our own two brand hues"]
- Any existing design tokens to reconcile with: [paste your current Color/Font extensions if any]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above, with a comment flagging the forest-text-on-bright-green rule.
2. A `Font` extension mapping the Wise Sans/Inter hierarchy including the uppercase-label tracking value.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the forest account hero (with number roll-up) and the fee-transparency breakdown card.
4. The mid-market rate ticker row and the send-money flow stepper component.
5. The bright-green primary CTA, forest secondary button, and a currency-balance row.
6. A short checklist mapping each house rule to where it was applied, so I can verify the fee-transparency and contrast rules held.
</what_to_give_me>
